answer_text:
Let

\[
L=\lim_{x\to 1}\frac{(1-x^{1/2})(1-x^{1/3})\cdots(1-x^{1/n})}{(1-x)^{n-1}}.
\]

There are \(n-1\) factors in the numerator, so we can rewrite the expression as a product of \(n-1\) quotients:

\[
L=\lim_{x\to 1}\prod_{k=2}^n \frac{1-x^{1/k}}{1-x}.
\]

Now evaluate each factor. Using L’Hôpital’s rule,

\[
\lim_{x\to 1}\frac{1-x^{1/k}}{1-x}
=
\lim_{x\to 1}\frac{-\frac{1}{k}x^{1/k-1}}{-1}
=
\frac{1}{k}.
\]

Therefore,

\[
L=\prod_{k=2}^n \frac{1}{k}
=\frac{1}{2\cdot 3\cdot 4\cdots n}
=\frac{1}{n!}.
\]

Hence,

\[
\boxed{\frac{1}{n!}}
\]

27B·v4.method: Linearize each factor (1−x^{1/k}) ≈ (1/k)(1−x) near x=1, take the product, and cancel (1−x)^{n−1} to get 1/n!.
